cases.customer_question: How can a product be registered when its intended qualification design references legacy Subset IDs that are no longer allowed under the current Bluetooth SIG registration system?
question_variants: Can old Subset IDs still be used in a new registration?
How do I replace legacy Subset ID references after the registration-system change?
Can I mix a module PHY QDID with different Host and Link Layer QDIDs?
What is the correct QDID strategy when old qualification references are no longer accepted?
How can an existing Nordic stack implementation be registered under the new system?
cases.actual_issue: A planned Bluetooth SIG registration relied on legacy Subset ID references that became ineligible under the post-July-2024 registration process, requiring a compliant replacement qualification design.
cases.plain_english_explanation: The product's Bluetooth architecture was based on previously qualified components, but some of the qualification references were no longer accepted by the updated Bluetooth SIG registration system. Instead of redesigning the qualification approach, an alternative set of existing qualified references was identified. This allowed the registration to proceed while still accurately representing the implemented Bluetooth solution.
cases.consultant_answer: The consultant determined that the desired legacy Subset-ID-based registration path could not be used under the current registration rules. A replacement qualification structure was identified using an existing qualified Host Layer and Link Layer design corresponding to the implemented software version, while retaining the desired PHY Layer implementation. This combination produced a valid registration path and preserved the intended architecture without requiring a new qualification design.
cases.decision_logic: When a qualification reference becomes ineligible due to registration-rule changes, the correct approach is to locate an equivalent qualified design that accurately represents the implementation and is accepted by the current registration system. Compliance with current QDID-reference rules takes precedence over historical registration practices.
cases.final_recommendation: Review all planned QDID references against current Bluetooth SIG registration rules and replace unsupported legacy Subset-ID references with eligible qualified designs before creating the final registration project.
cases.risk_if_done_wrong: Using ineligible qualification references can prevent successful registration, create registration-review issues, require qualification redesign, and delay declaration completion.
